question: With a fixed readout and an estimator that refuses to infer goals from undirected or distance-insensitive behavior, do fresh policies reveal the same goal type across the three same-task batteries?
readout: sample actions from the unchanged policy softmax (temperature 1, as trained), 32 rollouts per trial, horizon 20; greedy argmax reported as secondary

estimator.interval: 95% profile likelihood on delta_star, never narrower than +-0.5 (integer gaps)
estimator.set_on: development batteries (63001-63004) and known controls only; slack chosen so a 20%-random-action agent passes and a random walk fails

training.platform_note: trained in the cloud workspace (x86_64, jax 0.4.35); Test 3 weights do not reproduce bit-for-bit across platforms

primary.P1_measurement_valid: on all three confirmation batteries: optimal controls w in {0.15,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.85} with eps in {0,0.1,0.2}, and soft_optimal w in {0.3,0.7} tau 2, each have true w inside the interval and |w_hat - w| <= 0.03; the 50/50 mixture is distance_insensitive; the random walk is insufficiently_directed
primary.P3_stability: eligible = policy not insufficiently_directed on the original battery. A pair (policy, battery in {reflected, distance_reweighted}) agrees if the type matches and, for trade_off, the w intervals overlap. Agreement rate over eligible pairs >= 0.90: stable; <= 0.70: unstable; otherwise inconclusive. Fewer than 4 eligible policies: inconclusive. Interpreted only if P1 passes.

secondary: eligibility under v2 vs the Test 3 greedy gate (equal-distance neither <= 10%) on the same fresh policies
legacy revpref weight for the random control
per-policy types by cohort; no cohort-mean goal claims
